title: 2016 AMC12B 24
statement: There are exactly \(77{,}000\) ordered quadruples \((a,b,c,d)\) such that \(\gcd(a,b,c,d)=77\) and \(\text{lcm}(a,b,c,d)=n.\) What is the smallest possible value of \(n?\)

solutions.text:
Writing each entry as \(77\) times a reduced value, we need \(\gcd=1\) and \(\text{lcm}=m=\frac{n}{77}.\) For each prime \(p\) dividing \(m\) with maximum exponent \(M,\) the number of valid exponent quadruples is \((M+1)^4-2M^4\) \(+(M-1)^4\) \(=2(6M^2+1).\) The total over all primes must equal \(77{,}000=2^3\cdot5^3\cdot7\cdot11.\) Since \(2(6M^2+1)\) equals \(14,\) \(50,\) and \(110\) for \(M=1,2,3,\) and \(14\cdot50\cdot110=77{,}000,\) the exponents \(1,2,3\) give one candidate factorization.

Every prime contributes exactly one factor of \(2,\) so exactly three primes divide \(m.\) Their odd factors \(6M^2+1\) must divide \(\frac{77{,}000}{2^3}=9625.\) Checking the divisors gives \(M=1,2,3,8,\) with odd factors \(7,25,55,385.\) The choice \(M=8\) leaves only \(25\) for the product of the other two odd factors, but each is at least \(7,\) so this is impossible. Therefore the maximum exponents are exactly \(1,2,3.\) To minimize \(m=\frac{n}{77},\) assign the largest exponent to the smallest prime: \(m=2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5=360,\) so \(n=77\cdot360=27{,}720.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Divide everything by \(77.\) With \(m=\frac{n}{77},\) you need reduced quadruples of gcd \(1\) and lcm \(m,\) analyzed one prime at a time

For a prime with maximum exponent \(M,\) the count of exponent quadruples is \(2(6M^2+1).\) Use the factorization of \(77000\) to determine how many primes divide \(m\) and which values of \(M\) can occur
